summary: On 26 August 2026 ice and rock broke off high above the Lende Khola, on the Nepal-China border. The avalanche dammed the river; the water behind it burst through and ran about 100 km down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli as a wall of mud and boulders. Follow it downstream, point by point.

points.title: Where it began: the ice and rock collapse
points.what_happened: Ice and rock broke away from a glacier on the north side of Langtang Lirung and fell into the upper Lende Khola valley, blocking the river. ICIMOD scientists describe an ice-and-rock avalanche that dammed the river and then released a sudden surge. This spot lies outside this event's radar box: open the "Langtang Lirung glacier collapse" event to see what the radar measured there.

sources.label: USGS: 2026 Nepal debris avalanche and flash flood

points.title: Rasuwagadhi: the border crossing
points.what_happened: The Lende Khola meets the Bhote Koshi here, at the Rasuwagadhi-Gyirong crossing between Nepal and China. The flow tore through the crossing; buildings, the port area and the highway linking the two countries were buried or destroyed, on both sides of the border.

sources.label: USGS: 2026 Nepal debris avalanche and flash flood

points.title: Timure: the first village downstream
points.what_happened: Timure sits on the valley floor a few kilometres below the border, beside the road and the river. The surge overwhelmed the channel and the floodplain here before running on down the gorge.

sources.label: Maps of Nepal: anatomy of the Rasuwa-Tibet disaster

points.title: Syabrubesi: gateway to Langtang
points.what_happened: The trailhead town for the Langtang trek, where the Langtang Khola joins the Bhote Koshi. The flow passed through on its way to Betrawati and Trishuli Bazaar. Downstream, 11 hydropower stations and one solar plant, 431 MW in all, stopped operating, and UNDP estimated at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris. Reported deaths range from about 400 in early counts to more than 1,000, with thousands missing.
